notes.3a: (i) This question on the difference in melting points of two allotropes of phosphorus, white phosphorus (P ) and red phosphorus(P), is directly linked to their structures. White phosphorus (P ) is a simple molecule held together by covalent bonds between the four P atoms, whereas red phosphorus (P), is a giant three-dimensional structure of P atoms joined by covalent bonds. The melting point of the simple molecule, P , will thus be associated with overcoming the intermolecular forces of attraction, whilst the red phosphorus, P, will melt when the covalent bonds throughout the giant three-dimensional arrangement of the P atoms are broken. The few candidates who gave the correct structures for both white and red phosphorus tended to give a correct explanation for what was happening when P and P melted. Common errors included describing white P as ‘simple covalent’ and incorrectly comparing IMF’s in P with IMF’s in red P.

notes.4b: This question required the identification of a functional group (containing no O-H bonds), which is present, twice, in a product formed from the presence of a 2-hydroxyethanoic acid, in the reaction mixture. Two absorptions were given from an infrared spectrum of 1100 cm–1 and 1720 cm–1 linked to C—O and to C=O bonds. Many candidates correctly identified the functional group as an ester from the infrared absorptions. Very few candidates, however, went on to explain why one could eliminate the choices of alcohols and carboxylic acid functional groups as there were no O-H bonds, and deduce that an ester must be the only functional group present here, based on the IR data. A common error was for the mention of the presence of the alcohol and carboxylic acid groups, by stating what was in the Data Booklet for the absorptions 1100 and 1720 cm–1, identifying the presence of an O-H group, but then adding further comments that contradicted this statement.
notes.4c: (i) The reaction between 2-hydroxyethanoic acid and Na CO solution gave only the sodium salt of 2 3 the carboxylic acid functional group Many incorrectly suggested the alcohol group would also react with Na CO . 2 3
notes.4cii: The reduction of the hydroxy acid to the diol, (CH OH) , can be achieved using a strong reducing 2 2 agent. (CH OH) 2 2 NaBH is a weak reducing agent and will not reduce the COOH group to an alcohol group.
notes.4d: The hydroxyl acid contains two polar O-H groups, thus interactions between hydroxy acid molecules include hydrogen bonding; water is a polar molecule that can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds. When the hydroxy acid and water are mixed the interactions between the hydroxy acid and water are hydrogen bonding, so the hydroxy acid dissolves in water. Many answers referred to the polarity of the individual but did not make the link of the interactions between the water and hydroxy acid and solubility in water. �PAGE�13
notes.key_messages:
It is important to emphasise to all students that, in questions requiring any form of calculation, it is often
unwise to round figures during the intermediate steps of determining a final answer.
Rounding errors for any mathematical numbers can be avoided if the process of rounding is left to the end of
a question, unless specified elsewhere in the question.
